planting.note: Plant in a sunny, well-drained site after the last frost; give it room to spread into a dense, weeping mound.

directions: Kiowa is a dwarf, weeping crape myrtle bred from Lagerstroemia fauriei stock at the U.S. National Arboretum, producing crisp white flower clusters on gracefully cascading branches through summer. Its light cinnamon-and-gray exfoliating bark and orange fall foliage give the compact shrub multi-season interest well beyond bloom time. The naturally mounded, weeping habit needs little pruning beyond removing dead or crossing wood in late winter; never shear or top it back hard, which destroys the cascading form. Its small mature size makes it a fit for foundation plantings, borders, or containers where full-size crape myrtle trees would quickly outgrow the space.

planting.note: Plant after the last frost in full sun with good air circulation to minimize powdery mildew.

directions: Velma's Royal Delight is a compact, multi-stemmed crape myrtle named for a Wichita, Kansas crape myrtle enthusiast, bearing dense panicles of vivid magenta-pink flowers from midsummer into early fall. Dark green summer foliage shifts to orange and red tones in autumn, adding a second season of color once the blooms fade. Its good resistance to powdery mildew and compact upright form make it a reliable choice for foundation plantings or smaller residential beds where full-size crape myrtles would be too large. Prune selectively in late winter to remove dead or crossing wood only; never top the plant, since this ruins its naturally tidy, upright silhouette.
